scenarios.basis: No protective credit until physical worst-case attenuation is established.
A correct sequence precheck cannot prevent downstream hardware excess RF.

claims.description: Sufficient passive attenuation prevents this selected excessive-RF event
A working limiter prevents the event without the shared protection dependency
A perfect sequence verifier prevents every excessive-RF event
Separate limiter and comparator faults are required for protection loss

interpretation: Passive attenuation remains in every cut set. The verifier can intercept software requests but does not prevent faults arising later in the DAC/amplifier. Shared protection causes bypass claimed independence. These tests do not simulate quantum dynamics, RF propagation, cryogenic thermal behavior, or establish a SIL.
basis: Authored correction of the preserved gallery hazard model. Boolean event meanings and parameter scenarios are proposed teaching abstractions, not accepted field data.
